articles.title: Josh Brolin bought a 1.48-acre Georgia estate for $3.25 million in 2020; it was later listed for $4.999 million and rented for $35,000; after price cuts, the 7,700-sq-ft baronial home was sold for $4 million
articles.summary: In 2020, Josh Brolin bought a gated estate outside Atlanta for $3.25 million.
articles.body: In 2020, Josh Brolin bought a gated estate outside Atlanta for $3.25 million. It has now sold for $4 million, ending a listing run that opened at $4.999 million, with the listing pulled, the price cut and two attempts to rent it out.The 7,700-square-foot Sandy Springs baronial-style home sits on a 1.48-acre property. The Georgia home has seven bedrooms and 7.5 bathrooms. Though the final price is $999,000 under the original asking price, it’s still $750,000 above what Brolin, 58, and his wife, Kathryn Boyd Brolin, 38, originally paid for the estate.Three listingsThe ‘Dune’ star’s house first went on the market on April 17 this year, according to a report by Realtor.com. Three days later, it disappeared. Later, the listing resurfaced on June 8 with a $249,000 reduction from the initial asking price, bringing the ask to $4.75 million. The current buyer still got another $750,000 off.The Brolins also considered renting. The home was offered at $35,000 a month, first on March 5, 2024, and again on February 11, 2026. But neither attempt appears to have ended the search for a buyer.What the buyer getsWhen the Brolin family bought the estate, they hired design studio Pierce and Ward to give the home a traditional look with a heavy, castle-like feel. This aesthetic starts at the door: the marvellous 10-foot ceilings, striped wallpaper, classic crown moulding and wide arched doorways. The open-concept floor plan is the highlight. On one side of the entrance, you can see a formal dining room. On the other is a deep purple sitting room with coffered ceilings. The hallway runs back to a family room with built-in shelving and a large fireplace, one of four in the house.The kitchen opens directly off that space, with exposed wood beams, lantern-style lighting, a breakfast nook and a walk-in pantry. The massive mansion also has a dedicated laundry room, office area, screened porch and a large garage close by.The primary suite is located on the ground floor, with cathedral ceilings and green wallpaper. Its bathroom has dual vanities and a soaking tub set before an arched window.Downstairs, the basement holds a home theatre, gym, den and a bedroom with its own bath. Three more bedrooms and two sitting areas fill the second floor. A two-level guesthouse adds the remaining bedrooms and a second kitchen. Outside, a lagoon-style pool anchors the landscaped backyard.Brolin wanted to move from the areaBrolin has been open about his feelings towards the neighbourhood. In a TikTok clip posted on May 2 by journalist DeWayne Hamby, the actor spoke on a panel at the Atlanta Film Festival about shooting ‘Weapons’ in the city. Working there kept him close to his two young children, he said, and he called that a ‘major plus’.“It’s an easy town. And what I love about Atlanta especially is it’s so diverse,” he said. Talking about the Sandy Springs home, he added, “We have a house in Sandy Springs, which I don’t particularly like. I just don’t. I’m just being honest. But downtown, like Inman Park and all that, I love.”He also shared what he really didn’t appreciate about the neighbourhood: “I like a little grit. You know what I mean? There’s not a lot of grit in Sandy Springs.”Though the area may not have been his favourite, the baronial-style home is perfect for those who like the neighbourhood. While the area may not have been his favourite, the Brolins certainly made the home their own, tapping celebrated interior design studio Pierce and Ward to decorate it with a traditional, baronial aesthetic.This Georgia sale lines up with his bigger move west. In February 2024, the Brolins bought a farmhouse in Santa Barbara, California, for $7.1 million. The first rental listing for the Atlanta home followed on March 5 of that year, roughly a month later.All this points to a family whose centre of gravity had already shifted. articles.title: Locals loot liquor bottles after truck crashes near Kharhat toll plaza in Araria district
articles.summary: Liquor truck crashes near Kharhat toll plaza in Araria, Bihar; bottles spill and locals allegedly loot cartons. Police seize truck, probe video, trace owner.
articles.body: Patna: What began as a road accident on a busy highway in dry state of Bihar soon turned into an unusual scramble for liquor bottles, as local residents allegedly rushed to loot a consignment of foreign liquor after a truck carrying the illegal cargo crashed into a road divider. The incident took place on Friday near Kharhat toll plaza on Araria-Raniganj main road under Raniganj police station in Araria district.The truck reportedly lost control, rammed into the divider and was badly damaged. The impact damaged the liquor cartons inside the vehicle, causing bottles to spill onto the road. Instead of gathering around to help after the accident, several locals allegedly began collecting the liquor bottles and cartons. What followed was a scramble, with people rushing towards the damaged truck, picking up bottles and carrying them away from the spot. A video of the incident also went viral on social media.The scene reportedly became chaotic within minutes. Women, elderly people and children were also seen among those allegedly collecting the bottles, according to the footage circulating on social media. Some people were seen carrying individual bottles, while others allegedly managed to take away entire cartons.The truck’s driver reportedly fled the spot soon after the accident. According to preliminary information, the driver may have realised that the vehicle was carrying liquor and left the truck before police arrived.By the time the police team reached the location, several bottles and cartons had reportedly disappeared from the vehicle by then.Raniganj police later brought the situation under control. Officers seized the damaged truck and the remaining liquor consignment.Sadar SDPO Sushil Kumar said police would examine the video footage and identify those allegedly involved in taking away the liquor. Action would be taken against anyone found involved, he said.“Police are also using the truck’s registration details to identify its owner and trace those allegedly involved in transporting the consignment. Investigators are trying to establish where the liquor was loaded and where it was to be delivered,” the SDPO added.Police are also working to recover the bottles and cartons allegedly taken away from the accident site.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Patna | Silver Rate in Patna | Bank Holidays in Patna | Public Holidays in Patna | Patna AQI | Weather in Patna | Petrol Price in Patna | Diesel Price in Patna | CNG Price in Patna | LPG Price in PatnaStay updated with the latest Patna news. articles.title: Eco-bag unit, solar panel system to boost sustainability in Ranchi
articles.summary: Ranchi Mayor Roshni Khalkho launches RMC’s eco-bag unit at Naga Baba market, flags 10 waste tractors, and commissions a 50kVA solar system for sustainability.
articles.body: Ranchi: In a major push towards environmental sustainability, Mayor Roshni Khalkho inaugurated a biodegradable polybag manufacturing unit at Naga Baba Vegetable Market on Friday, as Ranchi Municipal Corporation (RMC) rolled out multiple initiatives on Swachh Bharat Diwas on Friday to improve cleanliness and protect the environment.Set up by RMC, the facility is the first production unit established by any civic body in Jharkhand to make eco-friendly carry bags and curb the sale, buy and use of banned plastic bags.The unit will be run entirely by women associated with Area Level Federation (ALF), who will handle production, operations and marketing. Officials said the project is designed to promote environmental conservation, women’s economic empowerment and local entrepreneurial skills. Based on its performance, RMC may explore similar units in other city markets.The facility uses polybutylene adipate terephthalate (PBAT) and filler materials in a 7:3 ratio. It can produce about 40 kg of biodegradable bags per hour. Production cost is estimated at Rs 140 per kg, against a projected selling price of Rs 160 per kg, creating an expected surplus of Rs 20 per kg. Hourly sales may reach Rs 6,400, with a surplus of Rs 800.To strengthen sanitation operations, Khalkho and deputy mayor Neeraj Kumar also flagged off 10 tractor-trolley units procured through Union Bank’s corporate social responsibility (CSR) fund. “The 10 new tractors will enable more effective waste collection and transportation, particularly in view of the upcoming festive season,” Khalkho said.A 50 kVA hybrid solar panel system installed by Jharkhand Renewable Energy Development Agency (JREDA) was also commissioned at RMC headquarters. It powers the basement, ground, first and second floors, with scope to supply other floors, reducing bills and grid dependence and promoting greener, more responsible municipal administration.Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news. articles.title: 4 killed, 1 injured in two Ranchi road accidents
articles.summary: Four killed and one critically injured in two Ranchi road accidents; police probe crashes as traffic enforcement issued 95,665 challans worth Rs 6.47 crore.
articles.body: Ranchi: Four people were killed and another was critically injured in two separate road accidents in Ranchi district in the 12 hours since Thursday night, raising fresh concerns even as city police carried out enforcement against traffic violations, rash driving and illegal parking.In the first incident, a speeding car rammed into the rear of a trailer truck early Friday on the highway under Bedo police station limits on the outskirts of Ranchi. A man died, while another suffered grievous injuries.Locals said the driver may have either lost control of the vehicle or dozed off at the wheel. The trailer driver fled after the crash.DSP (Bedo) Deepak Kumar said police had seized the trailer and were trying to establish the identity of the deceased. “Preliminary information suggests the victims were from West Bengal,” he said.In another accident late on Thursday, three youths riding a motorcycle died on the spot after their two-wheeler collided with a truck under Kharsidag police station limits. The victims were travelling from Tupudana towards Rampur.Police identified one of the deceased as Loknath Singh, 30, while the identities of the other two were yet to be ascertained.The crash took place near an intersection where flyover and underpass construction is under way. Residents said frequent diversions, mixed movement of heavy and light vehicles, and poor road conditions have made the stretch unsafe.The fatalities come soon after traffic police concluded a month-long enforcement campaign from Sept 1 to 30. According to a police statement, 95,665 challans were issued and penalties worth Rs 6.47 crore were imposed for violations of the Motor Vehicles Act during the drive. Police also forwarded 38 cases to court for prosecution.Traffic police appealed to motorists to follow road safety rules, saying enforcement alone cannot prevent accidents unless drivers avoid speeding, reckless driving and other risky behaviour.Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news.
